text: A psalm of David. LORD, I call to you; hurry to me. Listen to my voice when I call to you.
Let my prayer rise before you like incense, the lifting of my hands like the evening sacrifice.
Set a guard, LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips.
Do not let my heart turn to any evil thing, to take part in wicked deeds with those who do wrong; let me not taste their delicacies.
Let the righteous strike me—it is a kindness; let him rebuke me—it is oil on my head; let my head never refuse it. But my prayer is still against the deeds of the wicked.

versions.text: Let the righteous strike me—it is a kindness; let him rebuke me—it is oil on my head; my head will not refuse it. But my prayer is still against the deeds of the wicked.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew אַל־יָנִי is a jussive (a wish or plea), not a simple future statement. Rendering it as "let my head never refuse it" preserves the volitional force and parallels the two preceding jussive clauses, which also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: When their judges are thrown down from the cliffs, then they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
Like ground broken and split open by the plow, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.

versions.text: Like ground broken and split open by the plow, our bones are scattered at the mouth of the grave.
versions.explanation: "Sheol" is the specific Hebrew term for the realm of the dead, which is broader than "the grave." Retaining it (with a brief footnote such as "Sheol: the realm of the dead") preserves the imagery of the underworld's open mouth.

text: But my eyes are on you, LORD God; in you I take refuge—do not leave me defenseless.
Keep me from the snares they have set for me, from the traps of those who do wrong.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets, all of them together, while I pass by in safety.

versions.text: Let the wicked fall into their own nets, while I pass by in safety.
versions.explanation: The word יַחַד ("together", "all at once") is not represented in the current rendering. Including it restores the completeness of the judgment described and adds a natural rhythmic beat to the closing line.
